title: Ridgeline Warranty Coverage Billing Standard: Reversal of Warranty Charges
content:
**Standard.** A Warranty Coverage charge is reversed in full, by one reversal that names it as its source, when the records show it was not owed under these terms: a no-defect trip charge on a claim later approved for the same component after a return visit, a no-show fee on a visit Ridgeline itself rescheduled, a fee charged twice for the same visit, or a transfer fee on a transfer the seller withdrew before completion. A warranty charge is reversed at most once. Charges correctly assessed are never reversed as a courtesy by support.

## Grounds that the records must show

| Charge | Ground for reversal |
|---|---|
| No-defect trip charge | the claim was later approved for the same component after a return visit |
| No-show fee | the visit was rescheduled by Ridgeline itself |
| Any fee | it was charged twice for the same visit |
| Transfer fee | the seller withdrew the transfer before completion |

## Form of a reversal

- It reverses the whole charge, in full, never part of it.
- It names the charge it reverses as its source.
- A charge that already has a reversal naming it as source is not reversed again; this is read from the system's warranty charge records.

## Cases (hypothetical)

1. A no-defect trip charge was billed; a return visit later led to the claim being approved for the same component. The trip charge is reversed in full, once.
2. A customer asks for a correctly assessed no-show fee to be dropped as a goodwill gesture. It is not reversed.
3. A fee was billed twice for one visit; one of the two entries is reversed in full, and that entry is not reversed a second time.
